application_review: PROGRESS. The preceding first-order concatenation round was rechecked before edits. Retained proof source hashes and axiom sets remain unchanged.

The dependent-selection theorem allows parameter types to vary with the stage and requires only nonemptiness. Selecting a bad parameter whenever one exists proves the uniform conclusion directly from convergence for every selection; no bounded finite-cardinality or countable-intersection assumption is introduced.

The weighted uniform-orthogonality theorem uses the actual unit-bounded selected families and original normalized nonnegative cell weights. Their pairings converge to zero because their Hilbert images lie in the tested submodule. The external test family needs only a uniform L2 bound.

Recursive inputs are products of two translated actual inputs. The nonroot image under Fin.succ remains nonempty and insertion of zero is always nonempty, so the original nonroot unit and structure hypotheses apply exactly. The original root input is not required to be pointwise unit bounded.

The second-direction positive-degree space preserves the shifted inputs and their products by the previously verified translation and structured-multiplication theorems. The lower-order actual mixed dual is both a first-direction generator and, by internal localization, a member of the second-direction space.

The actual mixed-dual representative is established separately with explicit function arguments. Splitting the construction and avoiding inference through the weighted L2 type alias resolved default-heartbeat timeouts; no set_option, increased heartbeat bound, additional axiom or weakened statement was used.

Every selected pair of stage/cell shift functions gives an actual recursive coefficient in the same intersection. The dependent uniform-orthogonality theorem therefore yields one eventual correlation bound valid for every pair of shifts at each stage.

Six theorems are audited. This proves recursive coefficient localization and uniform parameter testing against a family orthogonal to the lower intersection. A positive Gowers-norm testing threshold, full higher-order concatenation and qualitative Bessel remain missing. The original main target remains unproved.
